description: Fix retry bias in 7 metacognition notebooks (calibration, control, epistemic_humility, error_detection, fok, jol, learning_monitoring)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/docs/RETRY_BIAS_ISSUE.md for the fix pattern (strip think tags, parse locally, no retry LLM call)
Step 2: For each of the 7 affected metacog notebooks, open the corresponding task_*.py in repo/benchmarks/metacognition/

Step 3: Replace every schema= parameter usage and retry/except pattern with: single llm.prompt() call, _strip_think() helper to remove <think>...</think> tags, regex JSON extraction, local parsing — no second LLM call
Step 4: Update each corresponding .ipynb notebook to match the fixed .py file (sync notebook cells with .py source)
Step 5: Validate all 7 notebooks pass jupyter nbconvert --to notebook syntax check
Step 6: Run one quick smoke test (metacog_fok) against Bedrock Claude Sonnet to confirm the fix works end-to-end

description: Re-run all 9 metacognition benchmarks across 10 models with full Q&A transcript logging
steps: Step 1: Modify repo/scripts/run_benchmark_bedrock.py to save full prompt+response text per question per model (not just aggregate scores). Output to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/<benchmark>/<model>.jsonl with fields: question_id, prompt, response, parsed_answer, correct_answer, score
Step 2: Clear all cached .run.json files for metacog benchmarks in repo/results/ and repo/benchmarks/metacognition/
Step 3: Run all 9 metacog benchmarks sequentially across 10 models using the modified runner. Use 300s timeout per benchmark, 900s for DeepSeek-R1. Run models sequentially to avoid OOM
Step 4: Verify 89/90 transcripts exist (Ministral 3B calibration expected to fail). Spot-check 3 random transcripts for completeness
Step 5: Generate repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv from the new run

description: Per-benchmark analysis for external monitoring tier: canary, epistemic_humility, error_detection
steps: Step 1: Load Q&A transcripts from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/ for canary, epistemic_humility, error_detection
Step 2: For each benchmark compute: mean, std, range, ceiling/floor effects from score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv

Step 3: Review 5 Q&A transcripts per benchmark (pick: highest-scoring model, lowest-scoring model, mid-range model, one where score seems surprising, one random). Document: correct scoring examples, incorrect scoring examples, parsing artifacts
Step 4: Assess ground truth validity — are correct answers actually correct? Flag any debatable items with item IDs
Step 5: Write recommendation for each: keep as-is, revise specific items (list IDs), adjust scoring formula, or drop. Include rationale
Step 6: Save analysis to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/analysis_external_monitoring.md

description: Per-benchmark analysis for self-monitoring tier: epistemic_revision, learning_monitoring, control
steps: Step 1: Load Q&A transcripts from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/ for epistemic_revision, learning_monitoring, control
Step 2: For each benchmark compute: mean, std, range, ceiling/floor effects from score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv
Step 3: Review 5 Q&A transcripts per benchmark (highest, lowest, mid-range, surprising, random). Document: correct scoring, incorrect scoring, parsing artifacts
Step 4: Assess ground truth validity — flag debatable items with IDs
Step 5: Write recommendation for each: keep as-is, revise items (list IDs), adjust scoring, or drop
Step 6: Save analysis to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/analysis_self_monitoring.md

description: Per-benchmark analysis for prospective self-assessment tier: jol, fok, calibration
steps: Step 1: Load Q&A transcripts from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/qa_transcripts/ for jol, fok, calibration
Step 2: For each benchmark compute: mean, std, range, ceiling/floor effects from score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv
Step 3: Review 5 Q&A transcripts per benchmark (highest, lowest, mid-range, surprising, random). Document: correct scoring, incorrect scoring, parsing artifacts, BSS computation validity
Step 4: Assess ground truth validity — for calibration, verify procedural question answers are correct. For FOK/JOL, verify gamma correlation computation handles edge cases (zero denominators)
Step 5: Write recommendation for each: keep as-is, revise items, adjust scoring, or drop. Special attention to calibration floor effect (6/10 models score 0.000)
Step 6: Save analysis to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/analysis_prospective_assessment.md

description: Write metacognition track improvement plan based on per-benchmark analyses
steps: Step 1: Read the three analysis files: analysis_external_monitoring.md, analysis_self_monitoring.md, analysis_prospective_assessment.md from repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/

Step 2: Compile all revision/scoring/drop recommendations across 9 benchmarks into a priority-ordered list. Rank by: (a) impact on overall track discrimination, (b) severity of scoring bugs, (c) ground truth issues
Step 3: For each recommended fix, estimate effort (small: <30min code change, medium: 30-60min redesign, large: >60min with re-run needed) and whether model re-runs are required

Step 4: Group fixes into implementation batches: Batch 1 = scoring/parsing fixes (no item changes, no re-run needed), Batch 2 = item revisions (re-run needed), Batch 3 = benchmark redesigns (re-run + revalidation needed)
Step 5: Save improvement plan to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md with sections: Summary, Priority List, Batch 1/2/3 details, Remaining Known Limitations, Estimated Total Effort

description: Implement Batch 1 scoring/parsing fixes: JOL gamma variation penalty and Ministral 3B parse hardening
steps: Step 1: Open repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_jol.py. In the scoring function, after computing gamma but before gamma_norm, add: if np.std(confidences) < 1.0: gamma_norm = 0.0. This removes the free 0.50 gamma_norm score for models reporting constant confidence.

Step 2: Open repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_calibration.py and task_fok.py. In the JSON extraction helper, add a preprocessing step to strip triple-backtick-wrapped JSON before the existing regex extraction.
Step 3: Sync the changes to the corresponding .ipynb notebooks: metacog_jol.ipynb, metacog_calibration.ipynb, metacog_fok.ipynb in repo/notebooks/
Step 4: Validate all 3 modified notebooks pass jupyter nbconvert --to notebook syntax check
Step 5: Retroactively recalculate JOL scores from existing Q&A transcripts to verify impact. Record before/after scores for each model.

description: Add 10-15 difficulty-5 items to metacog_calibration to widen score spread above borderline std=0.083
steps: Step 1: Open repo/benchmarks/metacognition/data/procedural_calibration.py. Add 10-15 new difficulty=5 items: obscure mathematical constants (Catalan numbers, Ramanujan primes), multi-step logical reasoning with confidence traps, questions requiring meta-awareness of difficulty. Each item needs: question, correct_answer, difficulty=5.
Step 2: Update repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_calibration.py to include the new items. Verify difficulty weighting formula applies correctly with expanded set.
Step 3: Sync changes to repo/notebooks/metacog_calibration.ipynb
Step 4: Validate notebook passes jupyter nbconvert --to notebook

Step 5: Run updated calibration benchmark against all 10 Bedrock models sequentially (300s timeout, 900s for DeepSeek-R1). Save results to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/calibration_v2_scores.csv
Step 6: Compare old vs new std. Target: std >= 0.10. Record before/after score distributions.

description: Increase learning_monitoring rule difficulty from mixed 2-3 to 3-4 to widen accuracy spread
steps: Step 1: Open repo/benchmarks/metacognition/data/rule_systems.py and identify all rule systems used by task_learning_monitoring.py currently at difficulty 2. Raise to difficulty 3-4 by adding more complex transformation rules, longer chains, or less obvious patterns.
Step 2: Update repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_learning_monitoring.py if the difficulty parameter is set there rather than in the data module
Step 3: Sync changes to repo/notebooks/metacog_learning_monitoring.ipynb
Step 4: Validate notebook passes jupyter nbconvert --to notebook

Step 5: Run updated learning_monitoring against all 10 Bedrock models sequentially (300s timeout, 900s for DeepSeek-R1). Save to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/learning_monitoring_v2_scores.csv
Step 6: Compare old vs new std and range. Target: std >= 0.10, range >= 0.30. Record before/after.

description: Add 5-8 hard statistical fallacy items to metacog_error_detection to reduce 30% ceiling effect
steps: Step 1: Open repo/benchmarks/metacognition/data/error_detection_chains.py. Add 5-8 new difficulty=3 items targeting: ecological fallacy, Berkson paradox, multiple comparisons/p-hacking detection, survivorship bias, regression to the mean misattribution. Each needs: reasoning chain with subtle statistical error, error description, difficulty=3.
Step 2: Assign item IDs E45-E52 continuing from existing E44. Update the items list.
Step 3: Update repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_error_detection.py if item loading logic needs changes
Step 4: Sync changes to repo/notebooks/metacog_error_detection.ipynb
Step 5: Validate notebook passes jupyter nbconvert --to notebook
Step 6: Run updated error_detection against all 10 Bedrock models sequentially. Save to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/error_detection_v2_scores.csv
Step 7: Compare old vs new ceiling percentage and std. Target: fewer than 10% of models above 0.95.

description: Retry GPT-OSS-120B on metacog_epistemic_humility to achieve 10/10 model coverage
steps: Step 1: Check the Bedrock model ID for GPT-OSS-120B in repo/scripts/run_benchmark_bedrock.py MODEL_CATALOG
Step 2: Run metacog_epistemic_humility for GPT-OSS-120B only with increased timeout (600s) and reduced max_tokens if applicable
Step 3: If ValidationException persists, try: (a) reducing prompt length, (b) different Bedrock inference profile, (c) splitting into smaller item batches
Step 4: Record score in repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/score_matrix_metacog_v2.csv. If still failing after 3 attempts, document failure and mark as known limitation.
Step 5: Update repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/analysis_external_monitoring.md with the result.

description: Write IMPROVEMENT_LOG.md documenting all changes made during metacognition track improvement execution
steps: Step 1: Create repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/IMPROVEMENT_LOG.md with sections: Summary, Actions Taken, Items Changed, Scoring Changes, Re-run Results, Remaining Known Limitations
Step 2: For each fix implemented in prior tasks, document: what was changed (file paths), why (link to IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md priority number), before/after scores, item IDs added/modified
Step 3: Include a final score comparison table: old std vs new std for each of the 9 benchmarks
Step 4: List remaining known limitations not addressed and why (platform limitations, time constraints)
Step 5: Add final verdict: does the metacognition track now meet all quality criteria from GOALS.md Steps 2-3?
